title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the start of the axiomatic set-up of 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)', June 1986. It belongs to Grothendieck's search for a 'tame' or stratified geometry of figures, the 'topologie modérée' programme. There are two basic sets: a set M of 'multistructures' or 'multiplicités' (strata-like objects) and a set F of 'figures'. Page 2 sets up an incidence relation between M and F. Each figure F has a deployment Dépl(F) = F̃ ⊂ M, the set of multistructures incident to F. Each X ∈ M is itself regarded as a figure (1.2), so it has its own deployment X̃. From these one forms Fig_M(F) = {X̃ | X ∈ F̃} ⊂ 𝔓(M), a 'set-theoretic figure' in M indexed faithfully by F̃. M carries a partial order ≤; F̃ is a closed (i.e. down-closed) subset of M; and X̃ = {Y ∈ M | Y ≤ X} (1.5).

On this page:
(i) Because of this interpretation, the passage from F̃ ⊂ M to Fig_M(F) is completely evident. Grothendieck hesitates over whether the set-theoretic figure Fig_M(F) is really important ('mais à voir').
(ii) The two maps (1.3) let one identify a figure F either with a subset of M (via F ↦ F̃) or with a set-theoretic figure in M (via F ↦ Fig_M(F)).
(iii) In the first identification, the embedding M ↪ F of (1.2) becomes, by (1.5), the principal down-set map X ↦ X̃ = ↓X, from M into the closed subsets 𝔓_ferm(M).
(iv) Caveat: when figures are read as parts of M, the figure attached to a multiplicity X is not the singleton {X}. It is ↓X, the set of multiplicities bounded above by X: its sub-multiplicities, i.e. the multiplicities incident to X, or 'strates de X'.

Modern reading: M is a poset of strata ordered by 'lies in the closure of'. Figures are modelled by closed sets in the Alexandrov (down-set) topology of M. The map X ↦ ↓X is the usual 'closure of a point' (specialization order). The warning is the familiar fact that, in a stratified space, the closure of a stratum consists of that stratum together with all the strata in its boundary. The next page introduces a second order ≪ ('shadow', Multomb) built in the same way.
errors: In the bracket '[via F ↦ Dépl(F)]' for the identification with a set-theoretic figure in M, the intended map is F ↦ Fig_M(F); Dépl(F) = F̃ is the subset of M used in the first identification. This is a slip, either by Grothendieck or by the transcription.

Minor ambiguity: given 'à tel point évident, que …', the logic suggests 'ne me semble pas vraiment importante'. The handwriting appears to read 'me semble vraiment important(e) — mais à voir'. Either way it is a tentative remark, not a mathematical claim.

ideas.what: Identifying each multiplicity X with the down-set ↓X = {Y ≤ X}, giving an embedding M → closed subsets of M
ideas.modern_name: Principal ideal / closure of a point in the Alexandrov topology; specialization order; poset of strata with closure order
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937) for poset topologies; the specialization order is standard (e.g. Hochster)
ideas.where_published: Specialization of points appears in EGA I (0_I, 2.1). The 'multiplicités/figures' axiomatics appear only in these unpublished notes, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Two encodings of a figure: as a subset of the set of strata (its deployment) or as a set of subsets (Fig_M(F) = {↓X | X ∈ F̃})
ideas.modern_name: Incidence structure / encoding a stratified set by its face poset; set of closed strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in combinatorial topology (face posets, cell complexes)
ideas.where_published: Not published; it relates in spirit to the tame-topology programme of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6.

ideas.what: Warning that the figure associated to a multiplicity is its closure (the stratum plus its boundary strata), not the singleton
ideas.modern_name: Closure of a stratum = union of strata ≤ it (frontier condition)

missed.claim: This page belongs to an unfinished axiomatic 'analysis situs' based on two posets of multiplicities (≤ for incidence, ≪ for 'shadow'), with figures encoded as down-closed sets. The page itself contains only routine order-theoretic identifications. The interest lies in the overall unpublished axiomatic framework, not in this page.
missed.quote: la figure associée à X ∈ M n'est nullement {X}, mais X̃, ensemble des multiplicités majorées par X pour ≤
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It documents Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a combinatorial/poset foundation of tame topology, comparable to later work on exit-path categories and poset-stratified spaces (Lurie, Haine and others). That comparison would only be substantive if later pages develop it.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping: down-set/Alexandrov identifications and a caution about singleton vs. closure. Historically mildly interesting as part of the unpublished 1986 'multiplicités' axiomatics, but nothing new mathematically on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'le passage de F̃ ⊂ M à Fig_M(F)'; the ':' in the transcription stands for 'à'.
Possibly 'ne me semble pas vraiment importante' rather than 'me semble vraiment important'; the reading is uncertain.
'M → 𝔓_ferm(M)' (fraktur P, the closed subsets of M) rather than '𝓕_ferm(M)'.

'Donc il faudra être prudent avec l'identification dont il est question, entre X ∈ M multiplicités et des figures particulières'; 'alors' is likely not present, and 'avec' is an interlinear insertion.
'ensemble des multiplicités majorées par X'; 'ens[?]' is 'ensemble'.
Final words: 'ou encore des strates de X' (preceded by a struck-out symbol), not '∮ strates'.
